title: The thumbnail that lied
description: Automated screenshots captured the one second before each game became legible. Why a pixel-difference test cannot tell changed from recognisable, and the one-field fix.
summary: A capture tool that picked the earliest changed frame produced a duck game with no ducklings and a rhythm game showing MISSED. Fixing it meant letting each game declare when it is worth looking at.

title: Every check exists because it shipped
description: A tour of the automated gates that refuse to publish a game on this site, and the specific production bug that caused each one to be written in the first place.
summary: Blank canvases, frame rates reported as minus 134, a game you died in under a second, and forty lines of authoring notes pushed live. Each rule in the build gate has an incident behind it.

title: The play band
description: A portrait game stretched across a desktop window measured 3.2 times harder. Why the interactive region keeps a phone's proportions on any screen.
summary: Stretching a portrait game to fill a laptop screen does not just look wrong, it changes the difficulty. Keeping a fixed play band fixes that and makes vertical video clips free.

title: Nineteen games, zero players
description: Two weeks after launching nineteen original browser games, analytics read zero sessions and the ad application was rejected. A post-mortem on both.
summary: The technical checklist was complete and it bought nothing. The real failures were keywords nobody searches for and a catalogue with no identity, and the ad rejection was a diagnosis rather than an insult.

title: Making a game testable from outside
description: Twelve lines of read-only interface per game make twenty games checkable on every build. What the contract exposes, and how older games are handled.
summary: A game has no function to call and no return value to assert on. A small read-only global changes that, and reporting unjudgeable rules as skipped rather than passed keeps the green build honest.

title: A gate that graded the opposite
description: The quality gate demanded that a game end when idle. The new game must never end. Inverting the rule was easy; finding it wired to nothing took two weeks.
summary: Five new unit tests passed while the branch they covered was unreachable from any real game. A test that builds its own input cannot verify that anything produces that input.

title: Drawing felt without image files
description: How a wool world is rendered with canvas paths and no artwork at all: wobbled outlines, clipped gradients, one fibre tile over everything, and three attempts at fur.
summary: Felt photographs beautifully and behaves terribly as a sprite. Drawing it in code fixes the lighting problem and costs nothing in assets, once you stop drawing perfect shapes.

title: Progress you listen to
description: A game with no progress bar, where you check how far along you are by knocking on a seal and hearing how muffled it sounds. Every sound synthesised, no audio files.
summary: Filtered noise makes a convincing knock, and moving the filter cutoff with progress turns a status readout into something you feel. The finished state is warmer, not louder.
